points.t: Recurrent painful ‘boils’ in the same flexural sites, with double comedones, tunnels or rope-like scars.
Follicular occlusion and rupture, then IL-17/TNF-driven inflammation; obesity, smoking and genetics add risk. Not an infection or a hygiene problem.
Weight and smoking support, antiseptic washes, analgesia; topical clindamycin for mild disease; tetracycline course; early dermatology referral for biologics (NICE TA).
Under-treatment and delay: scarring and tunnels are irreversible. Also depression, and SCC in long-standing perianal disease.

points: **Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp** (perifolliculitis capitis abscedens et suffodiens)
Open/closed comedones (often **paired/"tombstone"**), painful firm nodules, abscesses, **draining sinuses**, rope-like scars.
Sites: **axillae**, groin, inframammary/submammary, buttocks, perianal/perineal, neck.
Typical case: recurrent axillary lumps since puberty → coalescent inflamed nodules, sinus tracts, pus, fibrosis ± smaller indurated nodules.

cards.name: Recurrent boils / carbuncles
cards.clue: Discrete pointing abscesses; less bridging tunnels/rope scars; culture may grow Staph

cards.name: Epidermoid / Bartholin cysts
cards.clue: Single cystic lesion; no multi-site comedonal disease

cards.name: Cutaneous / perianal Crohn
cards.clue: GI symptoms, fistulae; refer IBD work-up

items.t: Fluctuant abscess with **systemic upset**: same-day drainage.
**Hurley II–III** disease (tunnels, scarring) or failure of a 12-week tetracycline course: refer to dermatology for systemic or biologic therapy.
Low mood or suicidal thoughts: HS has a high psychological burden.
Chronic non-healing ulcer within long-standing perianal or buttock HS: exclude **SCC**.

pearls.t: Stop calling every axillary lump a “boil” after the third recurrence in the same fold — think HS.
Document **Hurley stage**, sites, smoking, BMI, prior antibiotics.
Pregnancy/breastfeeding intent changes antibiotic, retinoid, and biologic choices — ask early.
Abscess drainage alone is not disease-modifying.
